summary: Initial weight-first dissection found four screened parts (zero-based indices), spanning three functional labels: L24 MLP unit7144 month-name answer support (30.28% search-score drop); L22 MLP unit4840 numerator/denominator answer support (15.93%); L21 MLP unit540 fraction-role vocabulary support (19.15%); L15 attention head1 sign transport in product descriptions (20.16%, matched explicit-factor-sign control 2.53%). All passed hidden-held-out and five same-size random-part screening checks. The first three were subsequently audited by ablation against all later-added tasks, with negligible additional search-split losses. Weight evidence: month/fraction units have highly aligned output token families and matching gate-input projections; L15H1 has sign-preserving static OV maps and a multiplication-versus-division singular output direction, independently supported by attribution. Eight generated custom tasks were accepted. Strong weekday/parity/prime/Boolean token alignments often had little causal effect; sign MLP and delimiter clusters failed matched-control specificity; L20H10 product-sign candidate failed held-out. Month task baseline is only .00819, so its large relative drop is not evidence for robust calendar arithmetic. Scores are task-score proxies, not demonstrated accuracy reductions; no GSM8K confirmation was attempted.
